text: The G6, at least through Tracfone, does not. This difference makes the phone feel disappointingly insubstantial and light. The phone has great functionality, handling every app I throw at it with aplomb. Motorola's gesture support is really fun to use, allowing you to screenshot with a "3-finger salute", flick your wrist to activate your camera, or shake your phone like a Maglite to activate the flashlight. Another difference, weirdly enough, is in the charging ports. The G6 Play uses a USB micro connection, whereas the G6 uses the new "standard" (USB-C) that isn't as common as it likely will be in the future. That means your old micro USB plugs will not work. Sound quality is pretty good, although it could be a tad louder. Motorola tends to have a lot of complaints about faulty sound drivers in their phones, but thankfully this one avoided that curse.
I love the Moto G6. I'm very happy with the purchase. No complaints. Great phone, excellent camera.

Premium phone, discount price!. I've been using the Moto G6 for a few fays now and I'm impressed. My previous phone was an LG G4. The LG was a bit bigger and a lot more expensive, but I don't notice any appreciable difference in performance. The Moto G6 has much better cell and WiFi reception than the LG. The Moto screen is crisp and clear, and very responsive. All of the apps I used on the LG work flawlessly on the Moto. My only 2 issues so far are that the Moto does not have a user replaceable battery, and there is no easy way to rearrange the navigation buttons on the screen. However, at around $200, versus around a thousand or so for some of those so called flagship phones, I can live with a couple very minor inconveniences.

Nice cameras and yes, the airline app worked very well with the Moto G6. 8/10/2019: As of August 2019, the phone has been updated to Android 9.0 Pie. Along with the update, a couple of new apps were added too. Solitaire, Pandora, Wish, Yahoo Mail, and Tracfone’s Device Pulse are now part of the roster of preloaded apps. A small change that came with the update –and one I especially like, is that now you can take a screenshot by just pressing on the power button. The usual “Power off”, “Restart” options will appear, but now there is an “Screenshot” option too.
